rationale: Evidence: iteration 2 (best so far, 713.6) finishes the oval 20/20 and the s-bend 19/20. The slalom finishes 0/20, ends off track in every run, and reaches only 0.63 progress with about 1.05 line-loss events per run. Steering oscillation on the slalom is 0.31, so the loop is not jittering. The failure is the robot losing the line on the sharper bends and then drifting. The 5-sensor array spans only +/-2 cm, and a 16 mm footprint leaves the tape when the robot is more than about 2 cm off centre. Change: widen the sensor spread to +/-3 cm (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03), so the line stays under at least one sensor for larger errors. Weights must stay within +/-2 (the last attempt failed on -3), so I scale them to -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 for the new spread. That gives 0.67 weight per cm instead of 1.0, so I rescale the gains to keep the effective response per cm the same: kp 1.5 -> 2.25 (kp x weight-per-cm stays 1.5) and kd 0.6 -> 0.9 (kd x weight-per-cm stays 0.6). ki stays 0. base_speed, mass, body, wheel track, sensor size and y are unchanged so the effect is isolated. Expected result: line_loss_events on the slalom fall below 0.5, slalom progress rises above 0.8, and the first slalom finishes appear. Oval and s-bend should stay near their current results because the per-cm gain is unchanged. Hypotheses: (H1) a wider spread removes most line-loss events on the slalom; (H2) the gain rescale keeps steering_oscillation near 0.3 or below; (H3) if the slalom still drifts, the next step is to lower base_speed to 1.1 on the slalom-like bends. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, noise_robustness, per track.
